summary: Plan for the week of 2026-09-07: 29 Game(s), insights MISSING, 8 Post(s) in the last fortnight

games.name: Road Rumble
games.tagline: Pin the throttle. Throw the punch.
games.pitch: A Road Rash / OutRun style racing brawler on a pseudo-3D highway. Sprint against 5 rival riders over elevation crests and tight turns, dodge oncoming traffic, and throw punches or swing roadside clubs to stay on your bike and finish first.
hooks: We rebuilt 90s Road Rash in vanilla JavaScript with pseudo-3D raster projection.
Motorcycle racing with melee combat directly in your mobile browser.

games.name: Astra Duel
games.tagline: Counter divine astras. Chant for tejas. Loose the Brahmāstra.
games.pitch: A Rāmāyaṇa epic astra-duel. Counter Rāvaṇa's divine missiles with the true cosmic element before they collide, rhythm-chant authentic Āditya-Hṛdayam Sanskrit ślokas to restore your solar energy, survive the Śakti spear, and loose your Brahmāstra.
hooks: An epic Rāmāyaṇa astra duel game with authentic Sanskrit rhythm chanting in your browser.
Counter Rāvaṇa's divine missiles using elemental astravidya in this mythic action game.

games.name: Falling Blocks
games.tagline: Vibrant neon, pure flow state.
games.pitch: A neon falling-blocks puzzle in the spirit of modern Tetris. Features a 7-bag randomizer, hold slot, 3-piece next queue, ghost piece guide, SRS wall kicks, combo multipliers, and satisfying particle bursts.
hooks: The cleanest, distraction-free falling blocks game on the web.
No ads, no logins — just pure neon block stacking in 1 file.

games.name: Duo Quiz
games.tagline: How well do you actually know each other?
games.pitch: Two players, one phone. Answer each question for yourself, predict what the other person will say, then reveal together. Ten rounds that show where you are in sync — and where you have been guessing. Packs for new pairs, couples, friends, family and coworkers.
hooks: Predict how your partner answers — then find out how wrong you were.
The ten-question game that tells you whether you actually know your best friend.

games.name: Blind Spots
games.tagline: How you see yourself vs how they see you.
games.pitch: A playable Johari Window for two people on one phone. Each of you picks six words for yourself and six for the other — then the panes fill in: what you both see, what only you see, and the blind spots they see in you.
hooks: Find out your blind spots from the one person who actually sees them.
A 5-minute Johari Window you can play on a date.

games.name: Life Auction
games.tagline: 100 coins. Ten things people want from life. You can't fund them all.
games.pitch: A pass-the-phone game about what you value. Each player gets 100 coins to bid, in private, on ten things people want from life — then you reveal together and see where your priorities line up and where they collide.
hooks: Bid on what matters to you — then see what your partner bid on.
A ten-minute game that starts the money-and-priorities conversation without the fight.

games.name: Deep Talk
games.tagline: 36 questions deep — a guided dive for two.
games.pitch: Two people, one phone, a guided dive through three depths of conversation based on the 36 questions. Includes a real before-and-after closeness check-in so you can see what the conversation changed.
hooks: The 36 questions, as a game you can actually finish in one evening.
Measure how much closer you feel after 36 questions — the game does it for you.

games.name: Share or Take
games.tagline: Share or Take. The score says who won — the pattern says who you are.
games.pitch: Ten rounds of Share or Take between two people on one phone. Both share and everyone wins; one takes and burns the other; both take and it is mutual ruin. Round 4 pays double, round 7 is sealed, round 10 pays triple — and the pattern of your choices says more than the score.
hooks: How much do you trust each other, really? Ten rounds will tell.
Play the prisoner's dilemma with someone you love. Watch round 7.

games.name: Circle Quiz
games.tagline: Find out who in the circle actually knows you.
games.pitch: One friend takes the spotlight and secretly answers two questions about themselves while everyone else predicts what they said. The reveal is a knowledge map across the whole group — who reads whom accurately, and who has been guessing for years.
hooks: You have known them ten years. Two questions decide whether that is true.
The interesting number is not who won. It is who knows whom.
A quiz where every answer is one of your friends.

games.name: Group Blind Spots
games.tagline: One friend calling you stubborn is an opinion. Five choosing it is a portrait.
games.pitch: One friend steps into the mirror and picks six words for themselves; every other friend independently picks six for them. Where the choices agree and where they miss becomes a consensus Johari window — the things the room sees that you do not.
hooks: The words your friends pick for you, and the one you would never pick yourself.
A blind spot is not a blind spot until more than one person sees it.
A Johari window with the people who actually know you in it.

games.name: Who Said That
games.tagline: Everyone answers honestly. Then the room works out who said what.
games.pitch: Everyone secretly answers the same prompt, the answers come back shuffled, and the circle pins each one on its author. Reading the room correctly scores detective points; every friend you fool scores you chameleon points — so honesty costs nothing and being unreadable pays.
hooks: Anonymity makes people honest. Then you have to work out who was.
Two ways to win: read your friends, or be the one nobody can read.
The answer everyone assumed was his turns out to be hers.

games.name: Herd Mind
games.tagline: Think like the room, or wear the black sheep.
games.pitch: Everyone secretly answers the same prompt trying to match what most of the group will say. The biggest cluster scores and the lone answer wears the black sheep. Nothing personal is revealed, which makes it the round that gets a quiet group talking before anything riskier.
hooks: The point is not the right answer. It is the answer everyone else gave.
The round that gets a quiet table talking, before anything riskier.
Being the only one who said it is its own kind of prize.

games.name: Impressions
games.tagline: Answer as your friend. Then watch them answer for real.
games.pitch: Everyone plays the next person around the circle for three questions, then the real person answers the same three. The room sees the impression against the reality, arrow by arrow — how someone comes across against how they would put it themselves.
hooks: How you would answer as your friend, and how they actually did.
The gap between how you come across and how you would put it.
Everyone does an impression. Only one person can mark it.

games.name: Memory Lane
games.tagline: The only quiz your group can play, because you wrote it about yourselves.
games.pitch: Each friend secretly writes one question about the group's shared history, hiding the real answer among two decoys they invent, and then everyone plays the finished quiz. It sorts the people who remember the holiday from the people who have been improvising it for years.
hooks: A trivia night where the trivia is you.
Who remembers the holiday, and who has been making it up?
The decoys tell you as much about their author as the answers do.

games.name: Time Capsule
games.tagline: Seal tonight's predictions. Find out at the reunion who called it.
games.pitch: The group seals predictions about each other — who moves abroad, who goes viral, who is late to the reunion — and opens them together months later. It plays twice: once for the argument about what to write, and once when the answers actually arrive.
hooks: The game you finish months after you start it.
Write down who you think your friends will become. Check in a year.
Half of it is the argument tonight. The other half arrives later.

games.name: Chemistry Grid
games.tagline: A daily chemistry grid — name an element for every square.
games.pitch: Three criteria down, three across, nine cells, nine guesses — name a chemical element for every square before the guesses run out. Built for high-school chemistry.
hooks: Wordle for the periodic table.

games.name: Physics Grid
games.tagline: A daily physics grid: nine cells, nine guesses.
games.pitch: Three criteria down, three across, nine cells — name a physical quantity for every square. Vectors, SI units, dimensional formulae, and every answer revealed at the end.
hooks: The daily grid for people who remember their dimensional formulae.

games.name: Trigonometry Grid
games.tagline: A daily trigonometry grid on the unit circle.
games.pitch: Three criteria down, three across, nine cells — name an angle on the unit circle for every square, in degrees or radians.
hooks: Nine angles, one unit circle, one shot a day.

games.name: Organic Chemistry Grid
games.tagline: Nine cells, nine guesses, one organic compound each.
games.pitch: A daily organic chemistry grid: three criteria down, three across, and every cell wants a compound that satisfies both — alkane or acid, gas or solid, fuel or household product. When the guesses run out the reveal lists every compound that would have worked, which is where most of the learning is.
hooks: Name a compound that is both an acid and a household product. Now eight more.
The reveal teaches more than the round does.
Chemistry revision that behaves like a daily puzzle.

games.name: Energy Grid
games.tagline: Nine cells, nine guesses, one energy source each.
games.pitch: A daily energy-sources grid: three criteria down, three across, and every cell wants a source that satisfies both — renewable or not, burned or not, mined or drilled. When the guesses run out the reveal lists every source that would have worked.
hooks: Renewable and burned. Name one that is both, then do it eight more times.
The reveal teaches more than the round does.
A daily grid for the energy chapter nobody revises.

games.name: Carrom
games.tagline: Flick the striker, pocket the queen.
games.pitch: A polished arcade take on the classic Indian board game. Position your striker, aim with slingshot controls, and pocket your 9 carrommen and the red queen with realistic rigid-disc collision physics and a 3-difficulty AI.
hooks: The classic Indian board game Carrom recreated in pure vanilla JavaScript.
An AI opponent that calculates cushion bank shots in real time in your browser.

games.name: 8-Ball Pool
games.tagline: Real spin, called pockets, zero downloads.
games.pitch: Physics-driven 8-ball pool with full official rules, draggable spin control (topspin, backspin/draw, english), customizable felt themes, practice mode, 2P pass-and-play, and a smart AI opponent.
hooks: Looking for a quick 8-ball pool game at work without downloading an app or watching ads?
How to model cue ball spin and cushion restitution in vanilla JavaScript.

games.name: Tic Tac Toe
games.tagline: From 3x3 to nested 9x9 mind games.
games.pitch: Configurable strategy board game with two modes sharing one engine. Classic mode lets you play any N×N board (3x3 up to 9x9) with customizable win length k (Gomoku). Ultimate mode features a nested 9x9 grid where every move sends your opponent to a specific sub-board.
hooks: If you think Tic-Tac-Toe is too simple, try Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe where every move dictates your opponent's sub-board.
Play Gomoku or Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe against an unbeatable minimax AI.

games.name: Rocket Builder
games.tagline: Build a rocket from real parts, then see how high it flies.
games.pitch: Assemble a rocket from real parts — payload, tanks, engines, fins, avionics, boosters — learn what each one does, then launch and see how high your design flies. Cross the Kármán line to reach space.
hooks: Can your rocket cross the Kármán line? Build it and find out.

games.name: Car Builder
games.tagline: Build a car from 19 real parts and learn what every one of them does.
games.pitch: Build a car from 19 real parts — chassis, carburetor, alternator, driveshaft — and learn what every one of them does along the way.
hooks: Finally understand what an alternator does — by building the car around it.

games.name: Blackjack
games.tagline: Classic felt. 3:2 payout. Dealer stands on 17.
games.pitch: A polished, distraction-free Blackjack game with casino-accurate rules, chip betting ($5–$500), persistent bankroll, double down, and smooth 3D card flips.
hooks: Cleanest browser blackjack — no ads, no purchase prompts, real 3:2 payouts.

games.name: Knockout Football
games.tagline: 16 nations. 4 real stars each. Lift the trophy.
games.pitch: Arcade soccer set at the World Cup 2026 knockout stage. Choose from 16 real nations and authentic star players, control them directly with smart AI teammates, manage sprint stamina, curl charged shots into the top corner, and win the tournament.
hooks: Play World Cup 2026 knockout football directly in your browser with 0 loading time.
Control Mbappé, Messi, Bellingham, or Vinicius in this lightweight arcade soccer game.

games.name: Golf
games.tagline: 4 pristine holes. Wind, Magnus lift, flowing greens.
games.pitch: Full-3D golf over four authored holes rendered with Three.js. Features cinematic camera swoops, a 3-click swing meter with draw/fade timing, wind and Magnus-lift ball aerodynamics, sand traps, water hazards, and sloped putting greens with flowing break particle grids.
hooks: A full 3D 4-hole golf game running smoothly in your browser with wind and aerodynamics.
Check out how the putting green visualizes slope breaks with animated contour lines.

games.name: Drift
games.tagline: Grip is a budget. The battery is your life.
games.pitch: A bright, sunny endless drifting game with real weight-transfer and throttle dynamics — no handbrake. Drive a high-end EV across 4 procedural biomes, harvest zombie horde bounties, auto-park at EV fast chargers, and race daily seeded ghost lines.
hooks: A drifting game where the battery is your health bar.
We built a racing game with realistic weight transfer in a single index.html file.
When you pause this drift game, your EV actually uses auto-park valet to plug into a DC fast charger.

casual_gamers.name: Casual & Coffee-Break Gamers
casual_gamers.tone: Fun, frictionless, inviting, highlighting instant play and 0 loading time

web_developers.name: Web Dev & Engineering Community
web_developers.tone: Technical, deep, highlighting zero-dependency, single-file HTML, Canvas/WebGL, procedural WebAudio, WebRTC

indie_gamers.name: Indie Game Enthusiasts & Speedrunners
indie_gamers.tone: Gameplay-focused, mechanics-rich, challenging, emphasizing emergent physics and high-skill ceilings

board_and_puzzle.name: Strategy & Board Game Lovers
board_and_puzzle.tone: Thoughtful, tactical, comparing against classic physical rules and AI depth

friend_groups.name: Friend Groups, Families & Party Hosts
friend_groups.tone: Warm and specific about what the group finds out about itself. Brand rule 1 applies: lead with the relationship, never with the one-phone mechanic

students_and_teachers.name: High-School Students & Their Teachers
students_and_teachers.tone: Plain and unpatronising, treating the daily grid as revision that happens to be a puzzle; the reveal is the teaching moment

twitter.format: Thread or single tweet with media and punchy hook

facebook.format: Single post with engaging headline and link

campaigns.angle: the battery is the health bar

brandRules: Play-together Games: lead with what two people find out about each other, never the one-phone mechanic.
Never generic AI marketing: no rocket emoji, no "game-changer", no exclamation-mark hype.
Organic copy: at most two hashtags, and only after the link.
Honest copy only: no invented quotes, player counts, or awards.

limits.note: The X free tier is the reason for the write budget. The Strategist chooses the mix across Categories and Windows itself — there is no hard-coded balance.
